title: Source operational health must be independently expressible from coverage/output
requirement: An operator MUST be able to determine a source's operational health (is it reachable, erroring, blocked, stale) without that determination being silently affected by its coverage/output volume, and vice versa. A source producing zero new items in a period MUST NOT automatically read as 'unhealthy' purely because output is low, unless the Clank's own health model explicitly and visibly treats sustained zero-output as a health-relevant signal — in which case that must be a distinctly labeled dimension, not folded into one ambiguous score. This standard requires semantic separation, not separate pages: one screen or even one table MAY show both health and coverage together, provided they remain clearly distinct, separately-labeled dimensions. Coexisting on one surface is not itself non-conformant; conflating them into one blended metric is.
rationale: Directly evidenced by an incident in the fleet's own reference implementation: watch-clank's SourceHealth model was deliberately repaired on 2026-08-24 specifically because 'two dimensions a single state used to conflate' — it now carries acquisition_state (reachability) and yield_state (output quality) as separate fields on the same object. clank-architecture's own golden incident corpus (read-only reference) independently names this exact ambiguity as GIC-02, 'legitimate-zero source' — a source can correctly report zero items without being unhealthy, and the fleet has already had to learn this the hard way. Counter-evidence exists and is called out explicitly: korean-tech-wire's Source Health table literally mixes a health badge with a coverage count (latest_accepted) in the same table row with no distinct labeling, and smartphone-clank's /metrics page computes one combined health-score-and-coverage table with no separation at all.
forbidden: A single 'health score' or badge that is computed from a blend of reachability and output volume with no way to see which drove the result
Treating a legitimately-quiet source (nothing new to find) as equivalent to a broken source in the same status field
acceptance: Operational health (reachability/error state) and coverage/output can each be read as their own distinct, labeled value for a given source
A source with zero new items and no errors does not present identically to a source that is actually failing
If zero-output is itself treated as a health signal by design, that is stated, not merged silently into a generic status

evidence.summary: SourceHealth explicitly split into acquisition_state and yield_state, docstring states this repairs a prior conflation, dated 2026-08-24.
'Legitimate legitimate-zero source' named as its own incident class independent of this survey, corroborating the same ambiguity fleet-wide.
Both keep health and coverage as adjacent, separately-computed views; tablet-clank's Sources page caption states this explicitly: 'Membership... and current health are separate concepts.'

evidence.source: korean-tech-wire/dashboard.py:335 (Source Health table row includes latest_accepted); smartphone-clank/dashboard/templates/metrics.html:40-66
evidence.summary: Two current production counter-examples where health and coverage are genuinely conflated in one row/table.

notes: RATIFIED 2026-08-30 by Operator Ratification Decision 002 (decisions/0004-operator-ratification-decision-002.md). Version 2: requirement text made explicit that semantic separation, not separate pages, is what's required — chinese-tech-wire's and korean-tech-wire's coexistence of health and coverage data on one Health page is not itself non-conformant (only true conflation into one blended metric is; korean-tech-wire's same-row latest_accepted-in-the-health-table and smartphone-clank's combined /metrics score remain the flagged non-conforming examples). watch-clank and tablet-clank both satisfy this with adjacent fields on one row, which remains the recommended shape.
